title: [Flight] Avoid main-thread stalls from large debug strings

posted.message: This early return bypasses the existing `value.length >= 1024` branch that decrements `counter.objectLimit`. Before this change, large strings consumed the debug object budget; now strings over 1,000,000 characters emit a placeholder without consuming that budget, so a payload with many huge strings can still produce an unbounded number of placeholder entries and defeat the limiter. Consider applying the object-limit check/decrement before returning the placeholder, or duplicating it inside this branch.

title: RabbitProperties enables SSL even when spring.rabbitmq.ssl.bundle is overridden to an empty string

posted.message: This adds coverage only for `properties.getSsl()`. The PR description says the same empty-string handling is fixed for `RabbitProperties.Stream.Ssl`, but there is no corresponding production-code change or test in this diff. If `Stream.Ssl.determineEnabled()` still treats `bundle != null` as enabling SSL, `spring.rabbitmq.stream.ssl.bundle=` will continue to enable SSL unexpectedly. Please update the stream SSL logic and add a stream-specific regression test.

title: fix(http): preserve TLS options for proxy tunnels

posted.message: This cached tunneling agent now closes over the first `userHttpsAgent.options` via `originTLSOptions`. Because the agent is stored in `cache` and reused for matching proxy settings, later requests through the same proxy but with a different `httpsAgent` can still use the first request's TLS options for the origin. In the worst case, a request that used `rejectUnauthorized: false` can cause subsequent requests that expected normal verification to inherit that relaxed policy. Include the relevant `userHttpsAgent.options` in the cache key, avoid caching agents with per-request TLS options, or apply the TLS options from the current request rather than from the cached callback closure.

fix(http): preserve basic auth on same-origin redirects (#6929)

posted.message: This restores `auth` whenever the next URL matches the original request origin, even if a previous hop in the redirect chain went cross-origin. For example, `original.example` -> `evil.example` -> `original.example/sensitive` would send the original Basic credentials on the final request, letting the cross-origin hop steer an authenticated request back to the original origin. To preserve the intended “same-origin redirects only” behavior, consider comparing the redirect target to the immediately preceding request origin (available via `requestDetails` in `dispatchBeforeRedirect`) or marking the chain as credential-ineligible once any cross-origin redirect occurs.
